items.title: AWS shipped a local cloud emulator
items.oneliner: AWS finally shipped a first-party local emulator, giving agents and humans a cheaper way to test cloud code offline.

items.title: Weight editing boosted tiny model math
items.oneliner: MIT CSAIL says weight-space editing lifted Qwen3.5-0.8B math accuracy from 7.9% to 48.1% without retraining.

items.title: Apple outlined a Transformer-to-Mamba recipe
items.oneliner: Apple's two-stage distillation gets Mamba close to Transformer perplexity, making faster sequence models more practical to ship.

items.title: Voltage glitching unlocked an A100-class GPU
items.oneliner: A voltage glitch turned Nvidia's CMP 170HX into an A100-class card, exposing a hardware fuse model attackers can abuse.

items.title: Rust standard library had memory bugs
items.oneliner: Microsoft FORGE found memory safety bugs in Rust's standard library, a reminder that unsafe code still breaks safe guarantees.

items.title: GitHub Actions lockfiles got a push
items.oneliner: Locking GitHub Actions by digest is becoming table stakes, because mutable tags are still an easy supply-chain trap.

items.title: macOS Secure Enclave can hold SSH keys
items.oneliner: Storing SSH keys in Secure Enclave keeps private material off disk and memory, which meaningfully raises the bar on laptop compromise.

items.title: A false alarm nearly flooded Jane Street
items.oneliner: A false smoke alarm nearly drowned Jane Street's only NYC datacenter, proving physical failure modes still dominate uptime math.

items.title: Pomerado turns websites into MCP endpoints
items.oneliner: Pomerado claims any website can become an MCP endpoint, cutting browser-agent costs to cents if the reliability holds.

items.title: Atuin now syncs agent sessions
items.oneliner: Atuin Threads syncs and encrypts agent terminal sessions across machines, which fixes the growing problem of lost execution context.
